1375646.headlineEn: A lean, mean zombie ride — just short of Train to Busan
1375646.bodyEn:
I thought Colony was decent, but it is not in Train to Busan's league. The concept is interesting and the infected are presented in a way I hadn't seen before. The action beats and the zombie attacks are genuinely entertaining, and a couple of sequences land with real intensity.

The atmosphere and the creature design worked for me. The high-rise setting keeps the survival tension alive throughout, and the cast does a solid job across the board.

The film's biggest problem is the lack of depth in its story and characters. It never builds the emotional connection that Train to Busan earned, and a few plot points are predictable. Even with a strong concept, the film never fully cashes in on its potential.

Overall, if you like zombies, gore and survival action, it's worth a single watch — just keep your expectations in check. For me it was a decent one-time watch.

My rating: 7/10 — Go for it.

Platform: Theatres; Korean VOD on Wavve, Coupang Play, Watcha, Apple TV+ and others. No streaming in India yet.

Runtime: 2h 4m

Parental guidance: Strong gore, bloody violence, disturbing zombie transformations and mature themes. 18+ recommended.

1339713.headlineEn: A slow-burn psychological horror that earns its unease
1339713.bodyEn:
Obsession turned out better than I expected. This is not a typical horror film built on jump scares — its focus is psychological tension and a genuinely creepy atmosphere. It creates an uneasy feeling from the very first scene and lets the suspense build slowly. If you enjoy slow-burn horror, this one will keep you engaged.

The atmosphere is the best thing about it. The score and the cinematography work together to make every scene feel off. The lead performance is strong and the emotional beats land naturally. A few horror sequences are genuinely disturbing, and the film doesn't lean on cheap CGI or lazy scares.

That said, it is not perfect. The first half can feel slow and some twists are not as surprising as they want to be. The climax won't satisfy everyone. If you are expecting non-stop horror or action, you may be disappointed — but for fans of psychological horror, this is a solid watch.

Overall, it is not for everyone. If you enjoy dark, creepy, mind-game horror, it deserves one viewing.

My rating: 7/10 — Go for it.

1081003.headlineEn: A universe built on the wrong foundations
1081003.bodyEn:
I just finished Supergirl, and honestly, the new DCU Superman film was a genuine surprise — this one is not. The villain is the first problem: I assumed he was a subplot that would wrap up in twenty minutes before the real antagonist arrived. He never did.

Then there is the release strategy. A film arriving on VOD within 30–35 days is a red flag; even a moderately successful release normally waits 50–60 days, and bigger hits wait longer. This one clearly did not perform.

The script should have been rejected on the first read. The entire story could have been told in a two-minute flashback. There was no reason to build two hours of film around it.

As for Lobo — I am not deep enough in DC lore to know whether he was always written this way or whether James Gunn downgraded him, so I'll leave that to the fans.

What bothers me most is the order of operations. This universe is being launched sideways: no Batman, no Flash, no Wonder Woman. Get the Justice League leads ready before launching Superman's cousin.

The result is a flop. Let James Gunn direct films; building a universe is not a side project. And I could have forgiven almost everything if the villain had been strong. He wasn't.

My rating: 5/10 — Timepass. Wait for streaming.

Runtime: 1h 48m

Parental guidance: Superhero violence, some intense sequences and mature themes. Suitable for 13+.

1202033.headlineEn: Charming leads, but the mystery has run out of steam
1202033.bodyEn:
Enola Holmes 3 was a little disappointing. The mystery is not as gripping this time, and the story loses the playful, adventurous energy of the earlier films. It leans much harder into emotional drama and character moments, which pushes the detective thrill into the background. The opening and the ending work; the middle stretch drags.

Millie Bobby Brown is still excellent and carries Enola effortlessly. The Henry Cavill scenes are good, and the production quality, visuals and action hold up. The problem is the writing: too many twists are easy to guess and the climax doesn't land with much impact. Several times the film felt stretched beyond what the story needed.

If you're a fan of the franchise, it's worth one watch. If you're expecting the entertainment of the first two, temper that expectation — for me this is the weakest entry so far.

My rating: 6.5/10 — Timepass.

Runtime: 1h 48m

Platform: Netflix (English original, Hindi available)

Parental guidance: Mild action violence, some intense scenes, kissing and mature themes. Suitable for 13+.

1288420.headlineEn: Dark, intense and unapologetically adult — but it's a book, not a film
1288420.bodyEn:
A quick note first: as we discussed earlier, this is the first book of Pepper Winters' dark romance series Indebted — it exists as a novel, not a film.

Read from a reader's perspective, it is an intense, dark ride. I picked it up because dark romance and suspense thrillers are usually gripping, and it delivers a solid experience on that promise.

Don't come here looking for a conventional romance. The plot is dark, twisted and built on a revenge-cum-debt dynamic that hooks you from the opening chapters.

The biggest highlight is the psychological tension between Nila Weaver and Jethro Hawk. With tighter pacing it would be even more engaging — a few chapters in the middle slow down while the darker themes sit heavily.

Overall, if you enjoy dark romance and intense psychological thrillers, give it a try. It is not a sweet love story; it is raw intensity.

My rating: 7/10

Parental guidance: Dark romance themes, heavy emotional and physical control dynamics, intense adult situations and triggering content. Strictly 18+.

1630409.headlineEn: Thai action that delivers the fights, not the story
1630409.bodyEn:
This is a Thai film, and I watched it because their action movies are usually hard-hitting. It met that expectation and not much more — a decent one-time watch.

There is nothing new in the story. It is a standard revenge plot you have seen in plenty of action films before.

The biggest highlight is the action itself. The choreography is genuinely good. A shorter runtime would have made it more engaging; a few scenes feel unnecessary and drag.

Overall, if you enjoy action movies the way I do, give it a shot — watch it for the fights, not the story.

My rating: 6.5/10 — Timepass.

Runtime: 1h 58m

Platform: Netflix (Thai, Hindi dub available)

Parental guidance: Strong action violence, blood, crime and some strong language. Suitable for 16+.

969681.headlineEn: Grounded, practical and the best Spider-Man action yet
969681.bodyEn:
This was the first Spider-Man film I watched in a theatre, and honestly the experience was a lot of fun. Expectations were high, but I deliberately talked myself down the night before — matching No Way Home's hype is almost impossible.

That was the right call, because this film chooses a grounded Spider-Man story over multiverse spectacle. On that measure it is Tom Holland's best solo outing so far. No Way Home is still my personal favourite because of its sheer scale, and matching it would need another event of that size.

One thing I can say with confidence: the action here is the best Spider-Man action yet. The practical stunts Tom performs feel different on a big screen, and in 3D a couple of sequences genuinely felt like they left the frame.

There is also a moment involving Mr. Savage Hulk that I won't spoil. I'll just say seeing that version again after 2018 was a treat.

Don't treat this as just another MCU instalment. It feels like a proper Spider-Man movie, a feeling I hadn't had in four years.

I watched the Hindi dub and it was genuinely good — the comedy is written well enough that the jokes land in Hindi too.

My rating: 8.5/10 — Perfection. Highly recommended.

Runtime: 2h 24m

Platform: Theatrical release (Hindi, English, Tamil and Telugu)

Parental guidance: Superhero action violence, intense fight sequences, mild language and emotional themes. Suitable for 13+.

687163.headlineEn: An intelligent, emotional sci-fi story about hope
687163.bodyEn:
Project Hail Mary is a sci-fi adventure built around space, science and survival, told from the perspective of an astronaut alone on a ship. The concept is genuinely unique, and the science explanations and problem-solving sequences are what make the story engaging.

The first half can feel slow while the setup and memories unfold, but as the plot moves forward the excitement and curiosity build considerably.

In the middle and later sections an unexpected friendship becomes the emotional core of the story and connects the audience deeply to it.

The writing is simple but smart, which makes even complex science easy to follow. Overall this is an intelligent, emotional sci-fi story with a strong message about survival, friendship and hope.

My rating: 9/10 — Must watch.

Runtime: 2h 37m

Worth the cinema ticket? Absolutely — every rupee. Go experience it in a theatre.

Parental guidance: Mild profanity, no nudity. High-stakes survival rather than violence.

1213243.headlineEn: Style over substance — a three-hour test of patience
1213243.bodyEn:
Geetu Mohandas had the chance to build a unique world, Yash brings star power, and the cast is stacked — Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth. The final product, for me, is style over substance.

Watching Toxic felt less like being entertained and more like having my patience tested. You can appreciate the visuals and give Yash credit for screen presence, but the screenplay and storytelling damage the whole experience.

My rating: 3/10 — Skip.

Runtime: ~3h 14m

Platform: Theatres only (and honestly, save your money — this isn't worth a cinema ticket).

Parental guidance: 18+, with strong violence, bloody action, killings, drug-related content, abusive language, mature themes and some disturbing scenes. Not suitable for children or younger viewers.
